weightings.raster: Kontur Population as prepared in Phase 1
weightings.calibrated: hex residents rescaled so that district totals follow the district shares of employed residents in district_stats.csv (2025; source: taldau.stat.gov.kz GetIndexTreeData p_index_id=702840); the city total and the within-district distribution are unchanged

headline.sentence: Between 51% and 62% of residents - depending on how the population raster is calibrated - can reach fewer than 5% of city jobs within 45 min by transit (approximate network, a lower bound), concentrated in Alatau and Turksib.

companions: Between 59% and 65% of residents live within a 15-minute walk of the nearest clinic (r9; raster vs calibrated residents).
Between 77% and 81% of residents live within a 15-minute walk of the nearest grocery (r9; raster vs calibrated residents).
Between 48% and 55% of residents live within a 15-minute walk of the nearest kindergarten (r9; raster vs calibrated residents).
Between 8% and 11% of residents live within a 15-minute walk of the nearest metro (r9; raster vs calibrated residents).
22% of residents live within a 15-minute walk of the nearest park (r9).
Between 61% and 65% of residents live within a 15-minute walk of the nearest school (r9; raster vs calibrated residents).
caveats: Transit is approximate and a LOWER BOUND: OSM route relations with assumed speeds and headways; 55 routes with ordered stops are modelled and 122 of 712 inhabited r8 hexes host a modelled stop (DECISIONS D-044, D-047).
Car times are free-flow (no congestion): an UPPER BOUND on car access (D-046).
The mode gap divides a lower bound (transit) by an upper bound (car): it OVERSTATES car dependence and should be read as a ranking, not a level.
Jobs per hex are a model estimate (Phase 3 dasymetric surface), not a census.
Service counts and 2SFCA are hex-aggregated: they are analysed at the fine resolution only (D-049).

Deserts: population above its hex quantile AND access at or below the population-weighted access quantile (D-055). The README-literal rule (both quantiles across hexes) is counted beside every result as n_hexes_literal_rule; a measure without a meaningful low tail (free-flow car) reports no deserts.

LISA p-values are tie-aware two-sided pseudo p-values from seeded conditional permutations, so cluster counts are Monte Carlo estimates: `borderline` gives, per measure, the hexes within two standard errors of alpha that another seed could flip (on zero-heavy measures they flip in blocks). One test per hex also means multiple testing - the FDR counts are the conservative reading, and null where the permutation count cannot resolve them.

For many residents the modelled transit adds nothing over walking (share of residents with transit = walk job access, across the weightings: 100% at 15 min, 80% and 83% at 30 min, 43% and 50% at 45 min, 23% and 27% at 60 min); transit rankings and transit deserts partly measure where OSM lacks stop members.

2SFCA is zero-inflated (59%-67% of inhabited r9 hexes reach no facility within the catchment): its LISA can flag provision hot spots, but a zero among zeros is not statistically surprising and does not become a cold spot.

12 r9 hexes (37,028 raster residents) hold nearly all residents of their coarse parent although the neighbouring children are built up: an artifact of the residential-floor-area split (flag `point_mass`). They top rankings by residents - read fine-resolution ranks with that flag.

Residents per hex come from Kontur Population, a modelled raster that is skewed between districts: against the district shares of employed residents (source: taldau.stat.gov.kz GetIndexTreeData p_index_id=702840) it gives Turksib 1.51x and Auezov 0.42x their share (r9 grid). Every population-weighted result is therefore produced twice - `raster` and `calibrated` - and 2SFCA is recomputed with calibrated demand; `comparison` lists what changes. Absolute resident counts inherit the raster's undercount: prefer shares.
